label: Sharing Options, Reader Accounts & Access Control

questions.stem: Which data sharing mechanism lets you share with accounts in ANY region across clouds without manual replication, and can optionally charge for data?

options.text: Direct share
Listing
Reader account
Local view

explanation.correct: Listings let you share data with accounts in any region, across clouds, without manual replication, and can optionally charge for data, offer data publicly, and provide consumer usage metrics.

distractors.A: A direct share is limited to accounts in your region and cannot charge for data or auto-fulfill across clouds.
distractors.C: A reader account is a mechanism for non-Snowflake consumers, not a cross-region auto-fulfilling listing.
distractors.D: A local view is not a data sharing mechanism.

questions.stem: A direct share can share data with which accounts?

options.text: Any account in any region across clouds
Only reader accounts
Only accounts in a different region
One or more accounts in the same Snowflake region

explanation.correct: Use a direct share to share data with one or more accounts in the same Snowflake region, with no need to copy or move data.

distractors.A: Cross-region/cross-cloud sharing without replication is a listing capability, not a direct share.
distractors.B: Direct shares are not limited to reader accounts.
distractors.C: Direct shares target accounts in the same region, not specifically different regions.

questions.stem: By default, which role has the CREATE SHARE privilege required to create and manage shares?

options.text: SYSADMIN
SECURITYADMIN
ACCOUNTADMIN
PUBLIC

explanation.correct: By default, only the ACCOUNTADMIN role has the CREATE SHARE privilege. It can be granted to additional roles to delegate sharing tasks.

distractors.A: SYSADMIN does not have CREATE SHARE by default.
distractors.B: SECURITYADMIN does not have CREATE SHARE by default.
distractors.D: PUBLIC does not have CREATE SHARE.

questions.stem: Which THREE capabilities are available with Listings but NOT with a Direct Share? (Select THREE)

options.text: Share with accounts in your region only
Share without copying data
Auto-fulfill across clouds
Optionally charge for data
Optionally offer data publicly on the Marketplace
Read-only access for consumers

explanation.correct: Listings can auto-fulfill across clouds, optionally charge for data, offer data publicly on the Marketplace, and provide consumer usage metrics — none of which direct shares support.

distractors.A: Sharing within your region only is a direct-share limitation, not a listing-exclusive capability.
distractors.B: Sharing without copying data is common to both listings and direct shares.
distractors.F: Read-only consumer access applies to both mechanisms.

questions.stem: Which TWO options can a provider use to add objects to a share? (Select TWO)

options.text: Copy the objects into the consumer account
Grant privileges on objects to a database role, then grant the database role to the share
Grant privileges on objects directly to the share
Grant OWNERSHIP of the objects to the consumer
Attach the objects to a resource monitor

explanation.correct: A provider adds objects to a share either via a database role (grant privileges to a database role, then grant the role to the share) or by granting privileges on objects directly to the share.

distractors.A: Sharing never copies objects into the consumer account.
distractors.D: Providers do not grant OWNERSHIP of shared objects to consumers.
distractors.E: Resource monitors govern warehouse credit usage, not share membership.

questions.scenario: A provider wants to share data with a business partner who is NOT a Snowflake customer and does not want to sign a Snowflake licensing agreement.
questions.stem: What should the provider create?

options.text: A data exchange
A second Business Critical account
A reader account
A public Marketplace listing

explanation.correct: Reader accounts let providers share data with consumers who are not Snowflake customers, with no setup/usage cost to the consumer and no licensing agreement required from them.

distractors.A: A data exchange shares among Snowflake accounts you invite, not with non-Snowflake consumers.
distractors.B: Creating another Business Critical account does not give a non-Snowflake partner access.
distractors.D: A public listing targets Snowflake accounts, not non-Snowflake consumers.

questions.scenario: An administrator is documenting who bears the credit charges for compute used in a reader account.
questions.stem: Who is responsible for those charges?

options.text: The reader account's users pay Snowflake directly
The provider account that created and owns the reader account
Snowflake absorbs all reader account costs
The charges are split evenly between provider and consumer

explanation.correct: A reader account is created, owned, and managed by the provider account, which assumes all responsibility for credit charges incurred by users in the reader account.

distractors.A: Reader account users do not pay Snowflake directly; the provider is billed.
distractors.C: Snowflake does not absorb the costs; the provider pays.
distractors.D: Costs are not split; the provider bears them.

questions.scenario: A provider wants to cap the monthly credit consumption of warehouses in a reader account they created.
questions.stem: A provider wants to control reader account warehouse spend. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Reader account warehouses have a built-in fixed monthly cap
Warehouses in a reader account can consume unlimited credits, charged to the provider
Reader account usage cannot be limited by any means
A resource monitor can be set up to limit reader account warehouse usage
Reader account users are billed by Snowflake directly

explanation.correct: Reader account warehouses can consume unlimited credits (charged to the provider), so a resource monitor should be set up to limit usage.

distractors.A: There is no built-in fixed cap; usage is unlimited unless a resource monitor is configured.
distractors.C: Usage can be limited via a resource monitor.
distractors.E: Reader account users are not billed directly; the provider bears the credit charges.

questions.scenario: A team documents which SQL commands cannot be executed inside a reader account.
questions.stem: Which THREE commands are NOT allowed in a reader account? (Select THREE)

options.text: SELECT
SHOW WAREHOUSES
INSERT
CREATE SHARE
CREATE PIPE
USE WAREHOUSE

explanation.correct: A reader account cannot execute commands like INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, COPY INTO <table>, CREATE SHARE, CREATE PIPE, CREATE STAGE, and others; it is primarily for querying shared data.

distractors.A: SELECT (querying) is the primary allowed operation in a reader account.
distractors.B: SHOW WAREHOUSES is a read/metadata command that is allowed.
distractors.F: USE WAREHOUSE is allowed; querying requires a warehouse.

questions.scenario: An administrator creates a reader account using SQL.
questions.stem: Which command and object type are used?

options.text: CREATE READER ACCOUNT ... TYPE = SHARE
CREATE MANAGED ACCOUNT ... TYPE = READER
CREATE ACCOUNT ... TYPE = CONSUMER
CREATE SHARE ACCOUNT ... TYPE = READER

explanation.correct: Reader accounts use the first-class MANAGED ACCOUNT object. You create one with CREATE MANAGED ACCOUNT <name> ADMIN_NAME=... ADMIN_PASSWORD=... TYPE = READER.

distractors.A: There is no CREATE READER ACCOUNT command; the object is MANAGED ACCOUNT.
distractors.C: CREATE ACCOUNT with TYPE=CONSUMER is not how reader accounts are created.
distractors.D: CREATE SHARE ACCOUNT is not a valid command.

questions.scenario: A provider exceeded some limit and cannot create another reader account.
questions.stem: What is the default maximum number of reader accounts a provider can create?

options.text: Unlimited

explanation.correct: By default, the total number of reader accounts a provider can create is 20. To create more, you must contact Snowflake Support.

distractors.D: Reader accounts are not unlimited by default; the cap is 20.

questions.scenario: A provider drops a reader account to stay under the limit, then immediately tries to create a new one.
questions.stem: A provider drops a reader account to stay under the limit. Which TWO statements about deleted reader accounts are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: The dropped account is purged instantly with no waiting period
There is a 7-day retention period for deleted reader accounts
A new reader account cannot be created for 7 days after the drop (to replace it within the limit)
A replacement can be created immediately
The waiting period is 24 hours

explanation.correct: Deleted reader accounts have a 7-day retention period, and if you dropped one to avoid exceeding the limit, you cannot create the replacement reader account for 7 days.

distractors.A: There is a 7-day retention period, not instant purge.
distractors.D: A replacement cannot be created immediately due to the 7-day retention.
distractors.E: The period is 7 days, not 24 hours.

questions.stem: Which THREE DDL commands are supported for the MANAGED ACCOUNT object? (Select THREE)

options.text: ALTER MANAGED ACCOUNT SET TYPE
RENAME MANAGED ACCOUNT
CREATE MANAGED ACCOUNT
DROP MANAGED ACCOUNT
SHOW MANAGED ACCOUNTS
GRANT MANAGED ACCOUNT

explanation.correct: The MANAGED ACCOUNT object supports CREATE MANAGED ACCOUNT, DROP MANAGED ACCOUNT, and SHOW MANAGED ACCOUNTS.

distractors.A: ALTER MANAGED ACCOUNT SET TYPE is not among the supported DDL commands.
distractors.B: RENAME MANAGED ACCOUNT is not a supported command.
distractors.F: GRANT MANAGED ACCOUNT is not a valid command.

questions.scenario: An account administrator wants to let the SYSADMIN role create and manage reader accounts.
questions.stem: Which global privilege must be granted to SYSADMIN?

options.text: CREATE SHARE
CREATE ACCOUNT
IMPORTED PRIVILEGES
MANAGE GRANTS

explanation.correct: To delegate reader account creation/management, grant the CREATE ACCOUNT global privilege (GRANT CREATE ACCOUNT ON ACCOUNT TO ROLE SYSADMIN). Tasks require ACCOUNTADMIN or a role with CREATE ACCOUNT.

distractors.A: CREATE SHARE governs shares, not reader (managed) account creation.
distractors.C: IMPORTED PRIVILEGES is used by consumers to access shared databases, not to create reader accounts.
distractors.D: MANAGE GRANTS relates to granting privileges, not creating reader accounts.

questions.scenario: A consumer account administrator received a share that was built by granting privileges directly to the share (Option 2).
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about consumer-side access control are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: This option supports segmenting shared objects by role for different user groups
Consumers must be granted OWNERSHIP of the shared objects
The admin grants IMPORTED PRIVILEGES on the shared database to local roles
IMPORTED PRIVILEGES gives an all-or-nothing access to all objects in the share
Each consumer user must be added to the provider's share individually

explanation.correct: With direct grants (Option 2), consumer account admins grant IMPORTED PRIVILEGES on the shared database to local roles; this is an all-or-nothing approach granting access to all objects in the share.

distractors.A: Segmenting shared objects by role for different user groups requires database roles (Option 1), not direct grants.
distractors.B: Consumers are never granted OWNERSHIP of shared objects.
distractors.E: Provider adds consumer accounts (not individual users) to a share; user access is managed within the consumer account.

questions.scenario: A provider wants different groups of users in a consumer account to access only a subset of the shared objects, using a single share.
questions.stem: Which sharing option supports this segmentation?

options.text: Grant privileges directly to the share (Option 2)
Use a reader account
Grant privileges on objects to database roles, then grant each database role to the share (Option 1)
Segmentation is impossible with a single share

explanation.correct: Using database roles (Option 1), you segment objects by creating multiple database roles, granting each a subset of objects, then granting each role to the share. Consumers grant each shared database role to their own account roles for granular access.

distractors.A: Direct grants (Option 2) are all-or-nothing via IMPORTED PRIVILEGES and cannot segment by role within one share.
distractors.B: Reader accounts do not provide intra-consumer role segmentation of shared objects.
distractors.D: Segmentation is possible using database roles within a single share.

questions.scenario: A provider needs to share data from multiple databases (same account) in one share and considers using a database role.
questions.stem: Why can't the database-role approach (Option 1) be used for multiple databases?

options.text: Database roles cannot be granted to shares at all
Multiple databases cannot be in one share under any method
Database roles only work across accounts
The REFERENCE_USAGE privilege cannot be granted to a database role

explanation.correct: The database-role option can't be used for multiple databases because REFERENCE_USAGE (needed to include objects from multiple databases) cannot be granted to a database role. Use direct grants instead.

distractors.A: Database roles can be granted to shares; the limitation is specifically REFERENCE_USAGE.
distractors.B: Multiple databases can be in one share using direct grants (Option 2).
distractors.C: Database roles are scoped to their database, not designed to work across accounts.

questions.scenario: An administrator inspects shares using SQL to audit configuration and consumers.
questions.stem: Which TWO commands correctly report share information? (Select TWO)

options.text: SHOW GRANTS TO SHARE <name> lists object privileges granted to the share
SHOW GRANTS OF SHARE <name> lists accounts that have created a database from the share
DESCRIBE ACCOUNT <name> lists the objects in a share
SHOW SHARE OBJECTS lists consumer users
LIST SHARE ACCOUNTS shows provider credits

explanation.correct: SHOW GRANTS TO SHARE lists object privileges granted to a share; SHOW GRANTS OF SHARE lists all accounts for the share and indicates which have created a database from it.

distractors.C: DESCRIBE SHARE (not DESCRIBE ACCOUNT) describes the objects in a share.
distractors.D: SHOW SHARE OBJECTS is not a valid command.
distractors.E: LIST SHARE ACCOUNTS is not a valid command.

questions.scenario: A provider account executes ALTER SHARE sales_s ADD ACCOUNTS = xy12345 where the account xy12345 does not actually exist.
questions.stem: What is the outcome?

options.text: The command fails with an error about the missing account
The command completes successfully but no updates are made to the share
Snowflake creates the account automatically
The share is dropped

explanation.correct: When adding accounts to a share, if the accounts do not exist, the command completes successfully but no updates are made to the share; verify the account exists and the name is correct.

distractors.A: It does not fail with an error; it succeeds silently without changes.
distractors.C: Snowflake does not auto-create the account.

questions.scenario: A provider removes a consumer account from a share.
questions.stem: What is the immediate effect on that consumer?

options.text: The consumer keeps read access for 30 days
The consumer's database is converted to a local copy
The database they created from the share is instantly invalidated and queries stop working
Nothing changes until the share is dropped

explanation.correct: Removing an account from a share instantly invalidates the database they created from the share; all queries and operations on it stop working. Re-adding the account does not restore the old database.

distractors.A: There is no 30-day grace period; invalidation is immediate.
distractors.B: The database is not converted to a local copy; it is invalidated.
distractors.D: The effect is immediate upon removal, not deferred to a share drop.
